summary.text: Kevin Mullin is the Democratic incumbent for California's 15th Congressional District on the San Francisco Peninsula. A San Mateo County native, he ran a small communications business, served on the South San Francisco City Council and as mayor, and spent a decade in the California State Assembly, where he was Speaker pro Tem. He was first elected to Congress in 2022 and serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee.

paragraphs.text: Mullin was born in San Mateo County, California. His official biography calls him a fourth-generation Californian and San Mateo County native and the son of a high school government teacher.

He graduated from Junipero Serra High School in San Mateo, earned a bachelor's degree in communications from the University of San Francisco and a master's degree in public administration from San Francisco State University, and, according to his official biography, studied leadership at Harvard's Kennedy School of Government.

Mullin worked as an aide to Jackie Speier when she was a state legislator, and his official biography describes him as a small communications business owner (founder of KM2 Communications) and a television host and commentator.
He served on the South San Francisco City Council from 2007 to 2012, including a term as mayor in 2011.

Mullin represented San Mateo County in the California State Assembly from 2012 to 2022 and was Speaker pro Tem from 2014 until he left, which his office describes as the longest tenure in that role in the modern era.

His official biography says he had more than 60 bills signed into law as an assemblymember, including the DISCLOSE Act and Social Media DISCLOSE Act on political advertising disclosure, and that he helped create a $3.7 billion climate resilience package.
He also helped secure record levels of state child-care funding and streamlined the process for obtaining a child-care license.
Mullin won the November 2022 general election for California's 15th Congressional District over fellow Democrat David Canepa, 55.5% to 44.5%, and took office in January 2023.

In the 119th Congress he serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Energy; and Oversight and Investigations subcommittees. In the 118th Congress he served on the Natural Resources and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

His official biography says he is hard of hearing, wears hearing aids and has advocated for the deaf and hard-of-hearing community, and that he lives in the Bay Area with his wife Jessica and their twin sons.
